rule: Whenever a production validation pose or motion materially changes a matched joint/bone family, every listed coupling system becomes required review scope for that sample unless a candidate-bound evidence record explicitly demonstrates why that system is mechanically quiescent.

trigger_policy.material_motion: Use the project-owned rig/pose numerical precision to distinguish meaningful motion from floating-point noise; do not invent a new anatomical threshold merely to skip review.
trigger_policy.response_requirement: Required systems must be inspected at weights-only and final-corrected surface levels through outbound/intermediate/endpoint/return motion.
trigger_policy.quiescent_exception: A system may record negligible visible response only when both attachment continuity and the expected geometry for that motion are evidence-backed; absence of movement cannot be assumed from low vertex displacement alone.
trigger_policy.propagation: A distal contact or joint change also activates every proximal load/coupling chain explicitly listed by the matching rule.

rules.rationale: Head/neck motion distributes through cervical segments and changes neck/trapezius/trunk transition.
Trunk/pelvic motion changes ribcage-waist continuity and also changes proximal attachment state for shoulder, glute, groin, rectus-femoris and hamstring chains.
Clavicle movement changes trapezius/shoulder slope plus proximal pectoral and deltoid attachment state.
Scapular motion changes back drape, posterior axillary support, deltoid yoke and the chest/shoulder surface relationship.
Humeral motion moves distal pec/posterior-fold/deltoid attachments and changes the complete shoulder girdle surface, not just the arm.
Elbow and forearm motion affects upper-arm/elbow form, wrist load path and hand orientation/tendon chain.
Hand/wrist motion must remain continuous with forearm and finger tendon/palm surface.
Digit motion propagates through tendon/pulley/palm structures and loaded grip affects wrist/forearm.
Femoral motion changes glute, groin/adductor, rectus/quadriceps, hamstring and pelvic/trunk transition.
Knee motion changes extensor chain, hamstring/popliteal chain and gastrocnemius state; lower-leg alignment also affects ankle/foot load.
Ankle/hindfoot motion changes calf/Achilles continuity and heel/arch/forefoot contact.
Toe/forefoot loading must remain connected to arch/hindfoot and the proximal plantarflexion load path.

failure_rule: If a matched joint family moves in a validation sample and one of its required coupling systems is absent from candidate evidence, the sample is incomplete and cannot contribute to anatomical clearance.
